description:
A CNN panel sat down just weeks before the midterm elections to argue about a question neither side could agree on: which party is actually in trouble heading into November. What starts as a routine roundtable quickly turns into a sharp, high-energy debate about power, accountability, and whether the party controlling the government can survive its own record.

The disagreement splits the table cleanly. On one side, the argument is that the party in power is campaigning hard, touting real accomplishments on drug prices, deregulation, and innovation, and that any incumbent naturally faces an uphill climb in a midterm year. On the other side, the panel pushes back with polling, spending patterns, and the behavior of the candidates themselves, arguing that the party in power is quietly bracing for a rough night and running away from its own leadership.

The conversation moves through the issues voters say they care about most. The economy dominates, with the panel weighing inflation, the deficit, the national debt, gas and diesel prices, and the reality that a large share of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck. From there the discussion turns to immigration enforcement, a topic that once powered major electoral wins but has since become a serious liability, with polling showing a majority of voters disapproving of how enforcement is being handled. The panel also digs into what it means when a congresswoman in a heavily Latino district breaks publicly with her own party, an
